phases.name: Acceptance Criteria

phases.name: Specification
architectureDecisions: ADR-002 SQLite as the relational database
ADR-003 multi-page frontend without a UI framework
ADR-005 self-contained anti-automation instead of third-party CAPTCHA
phases.notes: No production code or tests written in this phase. No clarification required from a human.

phases.name: Implementation

firstWorkingHappyPath.evidence: Backend: POST /api/registrations returned 201 with the JSON backup present on disk. Full stack: a registration submitted through a real browser at http://localhost:5173 produced reference REG-20260921-ENTRG9BAPM, a JSON backup file, and both emails dispatched (captured by the json mail transport).

phases.filesModifiedNote: No pre-existing application files existed; the repository contained only experiment inputs and documentation.

dependenciesAdded.rationale: nodemailer was raised to >=10.0.10 and vitest to >=5.0.1, and exceljs transitive uuid was overridden to ^11.1.1, because npm audit reported 1 high and 5 moderate advisories on the first install. After the change npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.

implementationDecisions: Anti-automation runs before validation, so scripted traffic never reaches the database.
The JSON backup write happens inside the SQLite transaction: a failed file write rolls back the row and a failed commit removes the file [AC-005-04].

The backup file is written to a temporary name, fsync-ed through the writing descriptor and renamed, so an existing reference.json is always complete. The first implementation fsync-ed a read-only descriptor, which fails with EPERM on Windows; found by the Phase 3 smoke check and corrected.
Fields of the non-submitted variant are dropped during validation, so they can never be stored regardless of what the client sends [AC-001-13, AC-002-12].
Option identifiers that survive trimming are kept verbatim rather than discarded, so a malformed identifier is rejected as unknown instead of being silently ignored.
Rate limiters are mounted on exact paths, so the strict registration limit cannot throttle the configuration endpoint.
Emails are dispatched after the HTTP response and every failure is caught and logged [AC-005-05].

acceptanceCriteria.notVerifiableDetail: AC-G-14 (docker compose starts the whole system) and AC-G-16 (data survives a container restart) require Docker, which is not installed in this environment. security.note: No security defect was found in the implementation during verification. Separately, the first dependency install reported 1 high and 5 moderate third-party advisories; these were resolved during Phase 3 by version bumps and an override, before the affected code paths were written. They are recorded under phase 3 dependenciesAdded.
acceptedLimitations: Anti-automation replay cache and rate-limit counters are per-process; more than one backend instance would weaken both until a shared store is introduced (documented in specification 11).
TLS terminates at an upstream reverse proxy; TRUST_PROXY defaults to false and must be enabled only behind a real proxy.
No third-party CAPTCHA (ADR-005); a well-resourced attacker can still script submissions.

findings.description: Every HTML document served by the frontend container had no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. nginx add_header is not additive across levels: a location block declaring any add_header discards all inherited ones, and both document locations set Cache-Control. The proxied API location set no add_header and therefore still looked correct, which is why the static configuration review missed it.
findings.fix: Headers extracted into frontend/security-headers.conf and included explicitly in each document location with "always"; deliberately not included in the API location, which was also emitting a duplicate CSP.
findings.resultAfterReVerification: All five headers present on both documents, hashed assets and a 404; exactly one CSP on API responses. Regression-tested by e2e/container-specs/deployment.container.spec.ts.

findings.description: GET /api/registration-config was limited to 60 requests per 5 minutes per address and the global API backstop to 300 per 15 minutes. One page load costs one configuration request, so participants behind a shared public address consume one budget together: roughly 60 people opening the form within five minutes would lock out everyone else behind that address. Surfaced as intermittent container suite runs — 6 seconds and green on one run, 15 failures over 4 minutes on the next.
findings.fix: Limits made asymmetric by intent and environment-tunable: write path stays 5 per 10 minutes (the anti-abuse control), configuration raised to 300 per 5 minutes, global backstop to 1200 per 15 minutes. Reasoning documented in specification 11 and 12 and in .env.example so the values are not silently re-tightened.
findings.resultAfterReVerification: Three consecutive container suite runs at 46/46 in ~6.4s with no throttling; shipped write limit separately confirmed still enforced in the container (201 x5 then 429). Three new backend tests pin the behaviour.

testsAdded.backendDetail: 120 consecutive configuration reads are not throttled; a deliberately low configuration limit still throttles; the read defaults are asserted to exceed the write default.
testsAdded.containerDetail: e2e/container-specs/deployment.container.spec.ts: document security headers on both forms, on a 404 and on hashed assets; no server version banner; API reachable same-origin; API carries its own policy and not the document policy; backend headers survive the proxy; export refused without credentials.

correctness.acceptanceCriteriaNote: AC-G-14 and AC-G-16 were not verifiable during phases 1-6 because Docker was absent. Once it was installed they were executed and did NOT pass on first evaluation: two Major defects (F-06, F-07) were found in the deployment artefact and fixed. All 87 criteria are verified in the final state. Real SMTP delivery to a real mailbox remains undemonstrated and is recorded as such.

security.detail: Both found only by running the containers: F-06 (no security headers on any served HTML document) and F-07 (read-path rate limits denying the form to participants behind a shared address). Neither was in the application code; both were in the deployment artefact. Both fixed and regression-tested.
